title: Natural bounded-above point-sections comparison
statement: theorem point_sections_finite_reduction_iso (_hl : IsUnit (l : k)) : Nonempty (∀ (n j : ℕ) (_hn : 1 ≤ n) (_hj : 1 ≤ j) (hjn : j ≤ n), (pointFiniteReductionBoundedAbove k l E n).ι ⋙ pointFiniteReductionSections k l E n ⋙ pointFiniteReductionModuleTensor l E n j hjn ≅ (pointFiniteReductionBoundedAbove k l E n).ι ⋙ pointFiniteReductionSheafTensor k l E n j hjn ⋙ pointFiniteReductionSections k l E j)

proof.text: Good upper truncation and the reduced bicomplex total of a functorial flat resolution give a bounded-above flat complex mapping quasi-isomorphically to every bounded-above representative. Colimit preservation makes the total available; the categorical-flat/site-flat tensor comparison retains flatness of every term.

The ordinary comparison is an isomorphism of complexes and its pure tensor equation is preserved by the degree-zero mixed-tensor unitor. Sections are termwise flat. Both bounded-above flat complexes are K-flat, so the sheaf and module universal derived counits are invertible.

Compose sections factors, module counit, ordinary complex comparison, inverse target sections factors and inverse sheaf counit. Their naturality squares compose for chain maps. Represent any derived morphism by a right fraction and replace its middle complex by a bounded-above flat complex; cancel the invertible denominator to get naturality for derived morphisms. Transport along chosen model isomorphisms. A second application of naturality proves agreement on every bounded-above flat model.
